name: Cloudflare Zero Trust
description: Read-only Cloudflare Zero Trust access: Access applications, policies, groups and identity providers, Gateway rules, lists and locations, Cloudflare tunnels and service tokens

tools.name: list_access_apps
tools.description: List Cloudflare Access applications for the account (name, domain, type, session duration)

tools.name: get_access_app
tools.description: Get one Cloudflare Access application by its application ID

tools.name: list_access_policies
tools.description: List the account's reusable Cloudflare Access policies (decision, precedence)

tools.name: list_access_groups
tools.description: List Cloudflare Access groups (reusable include/exclude/require rule sets)

tools.name: list_access_identity_providers
tools.description: List the identity providers configured for Cloudflare Access on this account

tools.name: list_access_service_tokens
tools.description: List Cloudflare Access service tokens (client IDs and expiry only, never the client secret)

tools.name: list_gateway_rules
tools.description: List Cloudflare Gateway policies (DNS, HTTP and network rules) with action and enabled state

tools.name: list_gateway_lists
tools.description: List Cloudflare Gateway lists (domain, IP, serial number and other lists used by Gateway policies)

tools.name: list_gateway_locations
tools.description: List Cloudflare Gateway locations (DNS resolver endpoints configured for the account)

tools.name: list_tunnels
tools.description: List Cloudflare tunnels (cloudflared) for the account, optionally excluding deleted ones

is_deleted.description: Filter on deletion state: false for live tunnels only

name.description: Exact tunnel name to filter by

per_page.description: Tunnels per page (default 20, capped at 50 here)

tools.name: get_tunnel
tools.description: Get one Cloudflare tunnel by its tunnel ID, with status and connection timestamps

needs_review: RENAMED 2026-09-12 from id 'cloudflare_zero_trust' to 'cloudflarezerotrust'. A connector named 'cloudflare' is already registered, and a connector id may not prefix another id: every 'cloudflare_zero_trust_*' tool would prefix-route to 'cloudflare' (registry.js assertNoToolNameCollisions). The underscore-free id keeps the namespace safe. credentialType stays 'cloudflare_zero_trust' so specToEntry still maps to the vault entry of that key in services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js, whose fields (api_token, account_id) and Bearer testHeaders are what the scaffolded auth block reflects; auth was NOT changed.

account_id is a vault credential field, not a per-call input, so it rides in the base_url object template 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{{account_id}}' and every tool path is account-relative. The test block is /access/apps, which is exactly the live-tested testEndpoint the vault registry uses for this key.

base_url._probe substitutes account_id = '00000000000000000000000000000000', a nil 32-hex identifier: no account, nothing public, and never a credential. The hint exists because the generic dummy credential cannot route: curl 2026-09-12 with account_id 'QUOXSHAPEPROOFDUMMYACCOUNTID' answered HTTP 404 {"result":null,"success":false,"errors":[{"code":7003,"message":"Could not route to /client/v4/accounts/QUOXSHAPEPROOFDUMMYACCOUNTID/access/apps, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?"}]} at every path, an identifier rejection the harness would have to read as an unproven route. The runtime ignores _probe entirely.

Shape-proof 2026-09-12 is overall SHAPE_PROVEN: 12 of 12 probes proven (test plus all 11 tools), 0 AUTH_WALL, 0 AMBIGUOUS, 0 FAIL. Verbatim: every real path answers HTTP 400 {"success":false,"errors":[{"code":9106,"message":"Authentication failed (status: 400)"}],"messages":[],"result":null} while the control path /client/v4/accounts/00000000000000000000000000000000/quox-shapeproof-control-e4831a82 answers HTTP 400 {"success":false,"errors":[{"code":7003,"message":"Could not route to /accounts/00000000000000000000000000000000/quox-shapeproof-control-e4831a82, perhaps your object identifier is invalid?"}]}. Same status, different Cloudflare error code, so the differential proves host, TLS, base_url, the Bearer header and each route (flag differential_path_proof, control_error_code 7003). Note the contrast with the registered 'cloudflare' spec's proof, which is AMBIGUOUS: probing under an account scope makes the auth failure 9106 distinguishable from the routing failure 7003, where a bare /client/v4 probe is not.

Every response pick is documentary, taken from tools_source (https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/). No Zero Trust account was held for this draft, so no probe ever saw a 2xx and the field names, the {result, success, errors} envelope and the array shapes are unverified against live data. All 11 tools are GET and write:false; nothing in this spec can mutate Access, Gateway or tunnel configuration.
list_access_service_tokens returns client_id and expiry only. Cloudflare returns a service token's client_secret solely at creation time, so no read path can leak it, and none is picked.

Paging: the Access and Gateway list endpoints document no page/per_page parameters, so none are invented here. list_tunnels does document paging and its per_page is clamped to 50 (documented ceiling is 1000), a deliberate conservative cap for an agent-facing read, not an API limit.

Category set to 'cloud_hosting' to match the shipped taxonomy and the registered 'cloudflare' sibling. The scaffold's 'uncategorized' and the vault registry's 'zerotrust' are not buckets any shipped spec uses; the 12-value taxonomy has no security bucket.

Deliberately NOT shipped: /accounts/{account_id}/devices. Cloudflare has deprecated it in favour of the /devices/physical-devices surface, and shipping a deprecated read would age badly. Access users, seats and Gateway categories were also left out to keep the toolbox to the Zero Trust posture reads an agent actually asks for.
